designDeviationsFromCP1: geometry/drainage ended up as bespoke nested discriminated unions (ParcelGeometryState/ParcelDrainageState: {status,model|study} or {status,reason}) rather than routed through the generic FeasibilityFactState<T> present()/absent() spread helper -- that helper is built for small per-fact records; spreading a whole SitePlanModel/FloodDrainageStudy onto {status,...} was awkward and less readable than nesting under .model/.study. No behavioral difference from what CP1 described.

package-layer verdict/narrative/open-items/data-quality are computed EAGERLY inside composeParcelReportFacts (baked into the returned model) rather than lazily at render time. This surfaced in test design: a test that tried to mutate an already-composed model's jurisdiction post-hoc to exercise the FIPS-fallback narrative path no longer worked, because the narrative was already baked from the pre-mutation state. Fixed by composing a second model through the real path with the input actually varied (no county name in the descriptor) rather than hand-poking the output -- arguably a more faithful test than the original.

drainage composition is OPT-IN (options.drainage undefined by default) rather than automatic, to avoid silently turning every existing Site-Plan/X-Ray/unit-test caller into a drainage-study caller and to proactively address the WDLL's own named reversal-criterion risk (compose-the-whole-model cost blowup). The real engine-api Feasibility route opts in explicitly (drainage: {runWhenStale:true}); this was a design decision made during implementation, consistent with but more concretely specified than CP1's plan.
